data.cultural_impact: The name "Richhpal" holds a significant cultural impact in Hindu society, as it is derived from the Sanskrit language and conjures up various images of power, wealth, and leadership. The name signifies an individual who is rich in both material wealth and spiritual wisdom. Historically, this name has been borne by many celebrated kings, rulers, and literary figures who have left an indelible mark on Indian history.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Richhpal" lies in its roots in the Sanskrit language and its connotation of being rich in spiritual wisdom and knowledge. According to Hindu philosophy, the ultimate goal of life is to attain spiritual enlightenment, and the name "Richhpal" embodies this concept by suggesting a deep connection to the divine and a commitment to the pursuit of inner wisdom and growth. This name also symbolizes the idea of being a ruler of one's own mind, body, and emotions, and of using one's material wealth and resources to serve others and uplift the society as a whole.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Richhpal: Name of a deity, Rich or wealth, Pal or protector. One who guards and bestows wealth.

historical_references.reference: Richhpal was a famous Hindu king of the Sisodia Rajput clan, ruling the Mewar region in present-day Rajasthan, India. He is known to have ruled from 1422 to 1468 CE. He was a powerful and capable warrior, who expanded his kingdom during his reign.
historical_references.context: Medieval India, Rajput Clans, Mewar region

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Richhpal is found in the epic poem 'Ragamala' by the poet Surdas, where he is described as a great royal patron who supported poets and musicians, promoting the arts during his rule.
historical_references.context: Medieval India, Patronage of the Arts
